Description

POSITON SUMMARY

The Director of Development and Communications serves as a strategic leader responsible for designing, executing, and modernizing SAVE’s fundraising and marketing strategy to support our $4M annual operating budget. This role builds philanthropic partnerships, elevates organizational visibility, and leads a dedicated team. A primary mandate for this position is to assess and optimize existing internal workflows, establishing clear operational boundaries and transitioning the department toward high-performance, data-driven operations.

SUPERVISORY:
Development Associate, Grants Manager, and occasional external contractors

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Philanthropy & Fundraising (Estimated 70%)

Strategic Planning: In partnership with the Executive Director, defines SAVE’s overarching fundraising strategies, policies, and implementation; develops a robust, multi-year development plan encompassing major gifts, annual campaigns, and corporate/foundation partnerships.
Revenue Generation: Owns accountability for meeting the organization’s annual contributed revenue goals through events, direct major donor cultivation and oversight of department initiatives.
Board Engagement: Partners with and equips the Board of Directors in fundraising activities; serves as the primary staff liaison for relevant Board committees and provides timely, data-driven progress reports.
Campaign & Relationship Management: Oversees and advances membership campaigns, individual donor pipelines, and personalized cultivation and solicitation strategies.
Grants & Institutional Giving: Directs the strategy, tracking, and reporting for all corporate, foundation, and government grant proposals, ensuring compliance and alignment with organizational goals.
Systems & Data Management: Ensures donor tracking systems (CRM) and data workflows support the business needs of the organization; assesses and implements new technology as appropriate to drive data-informed decisions.
Events: Oversees strategic donor recognition and fundraising events to maximize engagement and return on investment.

Communications & Marketing (Estimated 30%)

Brand & Messaging Strategy: Develops and executes an annual marketing and communications plan to elevate SAVE's profile across digital, print, social media, and traditional press platforms.
Hands-on Execution: Oversees and directly contributes to the creation of digital and print content, including newsletters, social media, and website updates, ensuring quality control and brand alignment.
Cross-Department Collaboration: Educates internal teams on fundraising goals and serves as the brand steward to ensure consistent messaging across all organizational programs.

Leadership, Business Process & Financial Management

Workflows: Establishes clear operational lanes, guardrails, and internal workflows to define where development activities interface with communications initiatives; optimizes the collective capacity of the team to ensure revenue-generating activities are prioritized.
Operations Optimization: Directly guides and mentors the Development Associate in elevating fundraising operations, ensuring best-in-class donor data hygiene, gift acknowledgment workflows, and stewardship touchpoints.
Team Development: Recruits, supervises, and evaluates development and communications staff and independent contractors, fostering a collaborative and high-performing culture.
Fiscal Responsibility: Collaborates with the CFO and Executive Director to construct, monitor, and manage the annual departmental budget.

Qualifications And Requirements

Minimum of 8 years of progressive development and fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector, with a proven track record of securing major gifts and corporate/foundation funding.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in a related field. CFRE certification desired.
Change Management: Demonstrated experience in process optimization, workflow design, or scaling/rebuilding development and communications operations.
Relationship Management: Exceptional interpersonal skills with a demonstrated ability to build authentic relationships with diverse stakeholders, funders, and community partners.
Communication Skills: Superb written, oral, and presentation skills; ability to translate complex programmatic work into compelling fundraising narratives.
Technical Savvy: Proficiency with modern nonprofit CRMs/donor databases, digital fundraising platforms, and data analytics tools. Experience with agile content tools (e.g., Canva, email marketing platforms) is highly preferred.
Project Management: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing deadlines, prioritize effectively, and work both independently and collaboratively.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to walk; sit; drive; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to

stand; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions except when such accommodation would cause undue hardship.

The work environment includes settings of the client’s home, educational institutions, community places, and office environments. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions except when such accommodation would cause an undue hardship.

As an equal opportunity employer, SAVE supports equal opportunity for employment and advancement free of race, color, religious creed, ancestry, national origin, age, sex (including sexual harassment) pregnancy (childbirth or related medical conditions), marital status, sexual orientation (heterosexuality and bisexuality), medical condition (cancer and genetic characteristics), mental and physical disability (includes HIV and AIDS), political affiliation/opinion, Veteran’s status, or request for family leave. SAVE is committed to ensuring that the work environment of SAVE employees is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

Position Title: Regional Director Of Operations - Northern New England

Pay Grade: 17

Reports To: RVP

Salary: $130,000 - $140,000

Other Forms of Compensation:

With people as our core and a deep commitment to exceptional hospitality, CCL Hospitality Group has a philosophy rooted in caring for the individuals who care for our guests. Our most significant competitive advantage is our team members. We constantly strive to strengthen our service culture. Every team member knows they matter and owns a stake in our success, delivering hospitality excellence.

With four distinct operating companies – Morrison Living, Unidine, Coreworks, and The Hub, we are shaping the industry’s future leaders with a culture of service focused on elevated hospitality for community living across the country. Join us and discover how we drive mutual success that leaves lasting impressions.

Job Summary:

As the Regional Director of Operations, you will be responsible for the overall operation, growth, and profitability of the region. You will provide the vision and strategic leadership to drive resident and client satisfaction through the delivery of best-in-class dining and hospitality experiences. In this hands-on leadership role, you must have the ability to travel to regional communities to provide ongoing training and support to unit food and beverage leadership teams, quality assurance, and to identify areas of opportunity. This role requires a strong background in food and beverage management, exceptional financial management skills, building and leading diverse teams, and a passion for delivering outstanding resident experiences.

Account Management & Client Relations:

Balance company goals and regulatory agency requirements with individual client objectives to create a personal program that meets resident needs.
Conduct quarterly business reviews with client to make certain community objectives are being met, communicate industry trends, and ensure client has opportunity to share critical feedback.
Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned communities, or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the community.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced multi-site environment.
Flexibility to travel between communities within your region. Develop priority-focused consultation agendas in advance of visits. Ensure that community staff are given ample opportunity to schedule themselves to attend.
Drive guest satisfaction by maintaining product and service quality standards; Periodic property inspections, ensuring completion of company training programs and initiating corrective action as necessary.
Review resident surveys for service concerns and work with Executive Directors and the Director of Dining Services to address and resolve going forward.
Understand and leverage company support teams and systems to meet region Key Performance Indicators
Collaborate with department heads, executive chefs, restaurant managers, and other team members to create innovative menus and dining concepts that meet and exceed guest expectations.

Business and Financial Acumen:

Ensure responsible financial management of assigned communities. In partnership with leadership team, develop annual budgets to accurately forecast financial performance, monitor financial reports to ensure budgetary compliance, and implement policies to deliver financial results in accordance with those budgets.
Timely completion of all daily, weekly or monthly reports as outlined in the corporate policy and procedures.
Participate in the sales process by assisting with contract negotiations and leading new opening services for the transition of new business accounts.
Collaborate with marketing team to develop and implement promotional initiatives, special events, and marketing campaigns to drive revenue and enhance resident experiences.
Coach and support operations team to effectively manage wages and controllable expenses.

Team Building & Management:

Provide the vision, strategy, and tools to all team members to successfully execute their community dining program in order to exceed resident and client satisfaction.
Exceptional leadership abilities, with a demonstrated ability to motivate, develop, and manage a diverse team.
Provide both positive and negative feedback to department, team or individual staff members, identifying areas for improvement and implementing training programs, as needed, through onsite meetings, virtual meetings, telephone calls, one on one coaching.
Recruit, train, mentor, and motivate a high-performing team of food and beverage professionals, fostering a culture of excellence and teamwork.
Utilize an “open door policy” to solicit employee feedback and address team member problems or concerns.

Preferred Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in business, health care or related field, or equivalent comparable experience.
Confirmed ability to manage a team of six or more manager-level team members.
Minimum of two years’ experience in multi-unit management with a focus on Food Services.
Strong track record of driving customer satisfaction.
Proven ability to work effectively in an unstructured; fast paced and P&L environment.
Shown ability to mentor and develop team members.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

jobs.title: Global Executive Director, Studio Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We're Future, a global leader in specialist media. Our people bring our trusted brands to life, helping millions of people discover expert content that informs, inspires, and drives action. As a pioneering multiplatform media powerhouse, we provide expert content and technology that build valuable communities across all channels.

Description

The Executive Director, Studio Operations is the operational backbone of Future Studios and the chief of staff for the studio system. This leader owns studio operations, resourcing, traffic, budget partnership with Finance, utilization reporting, the studio operating rhythm and the cross functional interface with Legal, Compliance, Licensing, Rights, Brand Leads and Heads of Video. The role administers the studio's meeting cadence and converts strategy into throughput.

What You'll Do

You will report into the SVP, Future Creative

Own the global production operations system: intake, tiering, scheduling, resourcing and capacity management across US and UK hubs
Lead Production Management as function head: the Director, Production Management (US), the Senior Production Manager (UK) and their teams
Run studio budgeting standards, cost tracking and utilization reporting; partner with Finance on the studio P&L
Administer the studio operating rhythm: Studios Leadership Team secretary, production status, monthly business reviews and the quarterly OKR reset
Own the freelance and vendor network including rate cards, framework agreements, the freelance convertible pathway and quality management
Manage the cross functional interface: triage Legal, Compliance, Licensing and Rights items for productions in both regions
Manage studio facilities, kit, edit infrastructure and the production technology roadmap including DAM and AI workflow enablement
Own risk, safety, insurance and compliance across productions in both regions
Continuously improve unit economics: cost per asset, turnaround time and first pass quality

What You'll Bring

10+ years in production operations or production management at a studio, publisher, agency or streamer, with 4+ years at director level or above
Experience running operations across multiple markets or hubs, ideally US and UK
Deep command of budgeting, scheduling, resourcing tools and production finance
Track record standing up or transforming intake and capacity systems at scale
Vendor and facilities management experience including negotiation of framework rates
Calm, systems minded leadership under high volume delivery pressure

What We Offer

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
401k plus a company match
Uncapped leave
When we hit our targets, enjoy a share of our profits with a bonus
Refer a friend and get rewarded when they join Future
Well-being support with access to our Colleague Assistant Programs
Opportunity to purchase shares in Future with our Share Incentive Plan

The expected range for this role is $151,000 - $175,000. This is a hybrid role, working 3 days from the New York office.

Internal job family level Commercial 3

Diversity and Inclusion

At Future, we're working to attract, retain and foster diverse talent, educate our colleagues in the importance of diversity, and review our internal processes so that they remain as free from bias as possible. We recognise that, in order to reach diverse communities through our content, we must first ensure ours is a culture in which diversity can thrive.

Please let us know if you need any reasonable adjustments.

Lead the next chapter of one of Seattle's defining civic institutions.

Friends of Waterfront Park is seeking an accomplished executive leader to help shape the future of Seattle's waterfront, strengthen the organization behind it, and build the partnerships, culture, leadership capacity and financial foundation required for lasting public impact.
· Location: Seattle, Washington
· Reports to: Board of Trustees
· Search led by: ND Leadership Partners, Managing Partner Chris Nguyen

About Friends of Waterfront Park Friends of Waterfront Park is the nonprofit organization responsible for fundraising, stewarding and programming Seattle’s 20-acre Waterfront Park, a new public space stretching along the city’s central shoreline and reconnecting downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay. Working alongside the City of Seattle, Seattle Center, community organizations, cultural partners, philanthropic contributors and neighboring businesses, Friends brings the park to life through free arts and cultural programming, recreation and wellness, community events, public space activation, partnerships and ongoing stewardship. At its core, Friends works to ensure Waterfront Park is more than a physical place: it is a welcoming and inclusive civic gathering space where people and communities can connect with one another, Seattle’s waterfront and the stories and cultures that define the region.

The Opportunity Seattle's Waterfront Park is the product of decades of civic imagination, public investment, philanthropy, community engagement and partnership. Today, twenty acres of renewed public space reconnect downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay and bring together culture, recreation, nature, commerce and community.
With the capital campaign complete and the full park now open, Friends of Waterfront Park is entering a new institutional chapter. The opportunity ahead is to define the organization's long-term role, strengthen its internal and external leadership capacity, deepen civic and regional partnerships and build a durable financial model that sustains a vibrant, inclusive and welcoming waterfront for generations.
The Board seeks a President and Chief Executive Officer who can lead at the intersection of strategy, people, philanthropy, government, community and civic life. Staff emphasized the importance of a leader whose internal presence, communication, and values are as strong and consistent as their external visibility. The successful executive will build trust, communicate consistently, build leadership capacity, foster collaboration and create clarity while representing Friends with confidence across Seattle and the broader region.

The Executive Mandate The President and CEO will lead Friends through its transition from a successful capital campaign and park opening into its next era as an enduring civic institution. The President and CEO will shape strategy, advocate for Friends and Waterfront Park, steward a consequential public-private partnership, and build the financial and organizational foundation required for long-term impact.

Defining Priorities Build the Institution for the Next Era

Partner with the Board and staff to define Friends’ next chapter, establish clear strategic priorities, and strengthen the organizational capacity needed to deliver them. Foster an environment of trust, accountability and collaboration while ensuring the organization has the people, systems and resources to succeed.

Advocate for Friends and Steward a Complex Public-Private Partnership

Strengthen Friends’ position as a civic leader and trusted partner. Navigate government with political sophistication, advocate for the park and the resources needed to sustain it, build coalitions across public, private and community partners, and shape the next Management Agreement with the City.

Build a Sustainable Financial Model

Develop a diversified long-term financial model that strengthens philanthropy and donor engagement while expanding government support, corporate partnerships, grants, earned revenue and other mission aligned resources.
What Success Looks Like The Search Committee will evaluate candidates’ ability to advance the following outcomes:
·      Map a clear strategic direction guided by the Strategic Plan, as well as a focused set of priorities understood across the Board, staff and key partners.
·      Develop a diversified and sustainable financial model that supports public access, programming and long-term stewardship.
·      Cultivate Friends’ inclusive culture, and facilitate communication, growth and accountability among staff and leadership.
·      Deepen Friends’ relationships with key City and civic partners, secure the resources necessary to support the park and establish a successful framework for the next Management Agreement.
·      Ensure Waterfront Park remains a welcoming, vibrant and inclusive civic gathering place while Friends expands its impact and relevance across Seattle and the region.

Executive Competencies and Experience Friends welcomes candidates from nonprofit, public, philanthropic, cultural, higher education, economic development and other mission driven environments. Direct park management experience is not required. The Search Committee will place significant weight on how candidates lead and on the depth of experience they bring navigating complex, public facing organizations. The following competencies reflect the capabilities and experiences most important to success in this role.

Strategic Institution Visionary
[HT1] 
Sets direction and translates complexity into focused priorities, organizational capacity and sustainable execution. Creates the conditions for others to lead effectively.
Civic and Political Navigator

Navigates government and complex civic environments with political sophistication and sound judgment. Advocates effectively for Friends, Waterfront Park and the public resources required to advance their long-term impact.
Coalition and Relationship Builder

Creates alignment among people and institutions with different interests. Earns trust, communicates effectively and mobilizes public, private, philanthropic and community partners around shared outcomes.
Leadership and Talent Developer

Empowers strong leaders, establishes accountability and creates an environment of trust, collaboration, belonging and professional growth.
Financial Steward

Applies strong financial judgment and aligns philanthropy, government investment, partnerships, earned revenue and disciplined resource allocation to advance long term sustainability.
Inclusive and Resilient Change Leader

Leads with cultural humility, curiosity, courage and emotional intelligence. Understands context, makes difficult decisions and brings people through change with clarity and steadiness.
Leading the Next Chapter Friends has built significant community credibility, programming expertise, partnerships and institutional knowledge. The next President and CEO will be expected to understand and build upon those strengths while bringing greater strategic clarity and organizational maturity. The strongest leader will know when to listen, when to preserve what is working and when to move decisively to position Friends for its next era.

Why Friends of Waterfront Park This is a rare executive opportunity at the intersection of civic leadership, public space, arts and culture, community belonging, economic vitality, philanthropy and government.
The next President and CEO will inherit extraordinary momentum, a highly visible public asset, an engaged Board, talented and committed staff and a network of influential partners. They will also have the opportunity to help define the institution that supports the waterfront for decades to come.
For an executive who believes great cities are strengthened through shared public spaces, strong institutions, inclusive workplaces and authentic partnerships, this role offers the opportunity to leave a visible and lasting legacy.

$280,000 - $340,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications. Friends of Waterfront Park offers a comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined by the organization's compensation philosophy and the experience of the selected candidate.

Candidates will be evaluated through a structured process designed to assess executive leadership, strategic judgment, cultural competency, people leadership, relationship building, financial stewardship, governance partnership and the ability to lead through complexity and change.

Director of Operations

Georgia / Atlanta Cluster · DS Fitness

We’re growing fast, with nine gyms across two states already in the pipeline, and we’re hiring the operating leader who will make that build work. This is a builder’s seat, not a caretaker’s seat. You’ll take the operating system we run on our four Atlanta gyms, sharpen it into something we can trust and scale, and extend it as we integrate acquisitions and open new locations. This is your kind of role if you own a P&L by instinct, hold managers to a standard without being asked, and have run integrations or openings under a clock.

Reports to: 
Owner / Managing Member
Location: 
Metro Atlanta, in-field across all Georgia locations
Scope: 
5 Georgia gyms plus portfolio-wide financial ownership across all 9+ gyms in both states

ABOUT US

DS Fitness is a multi-unit Burn Boot Camp operator building toward and beyond a nine-gym portfolio across metro Atlanta and Upstate South Carolina. We run a disciplined operating model with a long-term institutional exit in view, and we care about financial rigor, accountability, and repeatable systems.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

·       The performance of the Atlanta cluster: five gyms, the GMs who run them, and the results they put up. You own how these gyms operate and grow.
·       Cluster NOI. It’s the number you’re accountable for, and you’ll have the authority to move it.
·       The financial backbone for all nine gyms: one set of numbers the whole group runs on, across both states.
WHAT YOU’LL DO

·       Run the gyms.
Spend real time in the locations, coach your GMs, set the standard, and hold it. Move each GM from “runs the gym” to “owns the P&L.”
·       Own the standard.
Set and hold the bar for member experience and facility standards across the cluster. Your GMs deliver it day to day. You make sure it stays consistent everywhere.
·       Own the number.
You’re accountable for cluster NOI. Drive membership, retention, conversion, and pricing across the gyms, and manage labor as a percentage of revenue.
·       Run a weekly cadence.
A standing operating rhythm and 1:1s on a scorecard, so every GM knows their numbers and you catch problems early.
·       Own the full SOP loop.
Spot the issue, build the fix, write the SOP, roll it out across the gyms, and hold each GM accountable for putting it in place within a set timeframe. Not just writing the playbook, but making sure the playbook actually gets run.
·       Use the data to stay ahead of problems.
Watch the numbers closely to catch issues as they start and correct them before they grow into real ones.
·       Find and stop the leaks.
The systemic ones that quietly cost real money: overstaffing, inefficient class schedules, missed transfers, sloppy promo execution.
·       Build the systems.
Own the SOP library, the reporting, and franchise and HQ compliance, so the cluster runs on numbers everyone trusts and nothing depends on someone remembering a rule. You own that financial backbone.
·       Open and integrate.
Lead the new locations openings and bring them and their teams up to standard. Each opening carries hard targets: presale goals hit by day 60, and at least 300 members within 90 days of grand opening.
·       Build the bench.
Own GM and staff hiring, onboarding, and retention.

WHAT YOU BRING

·       You’ve operated multiple locations and owned the results. You’ve carried a P&L, you read a number cold, and you notice when one looks wrong.
·       You lead people well. You hold managers to a standard and coach them to own their numbers without handholding.
·       You use data to catch problems early. You spot issues as they emerge and correct them before they become larger issues.
·       You’ve opened or integrated locations on a deadline, or you’re clearly ready to do so.
·       You’ve got the runway for this. Ideally seven or more years running multiple locations, and you’re ready to be in-market across metro Atlanta regularly, not running it from a desk.
·       You know membership or recurring-revenue businesses: churn, retention, conversion, and pricing.
No fitness background required. We welcome strong multi-unit operators from restaurant, retail, hospitality, boutique fitness, or any location-based service business. We’re hiring for the operating discipline.

WHAT WE’LL TEACH YOU

·       The Burn Boot Camp model, camp format, and programming.
·       Our tool stack (DOMO, POS and billing, franchise portal) and our specific SOPs.
·       The fitness product.
Not in this role: product standards, pricing strategy, capital, acquisitions, or vision.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

·       A trustworthy portfolio reporting layer and scorecard, built and live.
·       A GM accountability cadence that produces real P&L ownership across the cluster.
·       An acquisition integration executed to standard and the next new-location opening on track.

COMPENSATION

Target base of $120,000 to $140,000, plus a performance bonus of 20% to 30% of base tied to cluster NOI and the operating scorecard, with on-target earnings of roughly $150,000 to $175,000. Structure is weightable toward variable for the right operator.

Continuously improve unit economics: cost per asset, turnaround time and first pass quality

10+ years in production operations or production management at a studio, publisher, agency or streamer, with 4+ years at director level or above
Experience running operations across multiple markets or hubs, ideally US and UK
Deep command of budgeting, scheduling, resourcing tools and production finance
Track record standing up or transforming intake and capacity systems at scale
Vendor and facilities management experience including negotiation of framework rates
Calm, systems minded leadership under high volume delivery pressure

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
401k plus a company match
Uncapped leave
When we hit our targets, enjoy a share of our profits with a bonus
Refer a friend and get rewarded when they join Future
Well-being support with access to our Colleague Assistant Programs

Internal job family level Commercial 3

Friends of Waterfront Park is seeking an accomplished executive leader to help shape the future of Seattle's waterfront, strengthen the organization behind it, and build the partnerships, culture, leadership capacity and financial foundation required for lasting public impact.
· Location: Seattle, Washington
· Reports to: Board of Trustees
· Search led by: ND Leadership Partners, Managing Partner Chris Nguyen

About Friends of Waterfront Park Friends of Waterfront Park is the nonprofit organization responsible for fundraising, stewarding and programming Seattle’s 20-acre Waterfront Park, a new public space stretching along the city’s central shoreline and reconnecting downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay. Working alongside the City of Seattle, Seattle Center, community organizations, cultural partners, philanthropic contributors and neighboring businesses, Friends brings the park to life through free arts and cultural programming, recreation and wellness, community events, public space activation, partnerships and ongoing stewardship. At its core, Friends works to ensure Waterfront Park is more than a physical place: it is a welcoming and inclusive civic gathering space where people and communities can connect with one another, Seattle’s waterfront and the stories and cultures that define the region.

The Opportunity Seattle's Waterfront Park is the product of decades of civic imagination, public investment, philanthropy, community engagement and partnership. Today, twenty acres of renewed public space reconnect downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay and bring together culture, recreation, nature, commerce and community.
With the capital campaign complete and the full park now open, Friends of Waterfront Park is entering a new institutional chapter. The opportunity ahead is to define the organization's long-term role, strengthen its internal and external leadership capacity, deepen civic and regional partnerships and build a durable financial model that sustains a vibrant, inclusive and welcoming waterfront for generations.
The Board seeks a President and Chief Executive Officer who can lead at the intersection of strategy, people, philanthropy, government, community and civic life. Staff emphasized the importance of a leader whose internal presence, communication, and values are as strong and consistent as their external visibility. The successful executive will build trust, communicate consistently, build leadership capacity, foster collaboration and create clarity while representing Friends with confidence across Seattle and the broader region.

The Executive Mandate The President and CEO will lead Friends through its transition from a successful capital campaign and park opening into its next era as an enduring civic institution. The President and CEO will shape strategy, advocate for Friends and Waterfront Park, steward a consequential public-private partnership, and build the financial and organizational foundation required for long-term impact.

Defining Priorities Build the Institution for the Next Era

Partner with the Board and staff to define Friends’ next chapter, establish clear strategic priorities, and strengthen the organizational capacity needed to deliver them. Foster an environment of trust, accountability and collaboration while ensuring the organization has the people, systems and resources to succeed.

Advocate for Friends and Steward a Complex Public-Private Partnership

Strengthen Friends’ position as a civic leader and trusted partner. Navigate government with political sophistication, advocate for the park and the resources needed to sustain it, build coalitions across public, private and community partners, and shape the next Management Agreement with the City.

Build a Sustainable Financial Model

Develop a diversified long-term financial model that strengthens philanthropy and donor engagement while expanding government support, corporate partnerships, grants, earned revenue and other mission aligned resources.
What Success Looks Like The Search Committee will evaluate candidates’ ability to advance the following outcomes:
·      Map a clear strategic direction guided by the Strategic Plan, as well as a focused set of priorities understood across the Board, staff and key partners.
·      Develop a diversified and sustainable financial model that supports public access, programming and long-term stewardship.
·      Cultivate Friends’ inclusive culture, and facilitate communication, growth and accountability among staff and leadership.
·      Deepen Friends’ relationships with key City and civic partners, secure the resources necessary to support the park and establish a successful framework for the next Management Agreement.
·      Ensure Waterfront Park remains a welcoming, vibrant and inclusive civic gathering place while Friends expands its impact and relevance across Seattle and the region.

Executive Competencies and Experience Friends welcomes candidates from nonprofit, public, philanthropic, cultural, higher education, economic development and other mission driven environments. Direct park management experience is not required. The Search Committee will place significant weight on how candidates lead and on the depth of experience they bring navigating complex, public facing organizations. The following competencies reflect the capabilities and experiences most important to success in this role.

Strategic Institution Visionary
[HT1] 
Sets direction and translates complexity into focused priorities, organizational capacity and sustainable execution. Creates the conditions for others to lead effectively.
Civic and Political Navigator

Navigates government and complex civic environments with political sophistication and sound judgment. Advocates effectively for Friends, Waterfront Park and the public resources required to advance their long-term impact.
Coalition and Relationship Builder

Creates alignment among people and institutions with different interests. Earns trust, communicates effectively and mobilizes public, private, philanthropic and community partners around shared outcomes.
Leadership and Talent Developer

Empowers strong leaders, establishes accountability and creates an environment of trust, collaboration, belonging and professional growth.
Financial Steward

Applies strong financial judgment and aligns philanthropy, government investment, partnerships, earned revenue and disciplined resource allocation to advance long term sustainability.
Inclusive and Resilient Change Leader

Leads with cultural humility, curiosity, courage and emotional intelligence. Understands context, makes difficult decisions and brings people through change with clarity and steadiness.
Leading the Next Chapter Friends has built significant community credibility, programming expertise, partnerships and institutional knowledge. The next President and CEO will be expected to understand and build upon those strengths while bringing greater strategic clarity and organizational maturity. The strongest leader will know when to listen, when to preserve what is working and when to move decisively to position Friends for its next era.

Why Friends of Waterfront Park This is a rare executive opportunity at the intersection of civic leadership, public space, arts and culture, community belonging, economic vitality, philanthropy and government.
The next President and CEO will inherit extraordinary momentum, a highly visible public asset, an engaged Board, talented and committed staff and a network of influential partners. They will also have the opportunity to help define the institution that supports the waterfront for decades to come.
For an executive who believes great cities are strengthened through shared public spaces, strong institutions, inclusive workplaces and authentic partnerships, this role offers the opportunity to leave a visible and lasting legacy.

Compensation and Benefits The anticipated compensation range for the President and Chief Executive Officer is
$280,000 - $340,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications. Friends of Waterfront Park offers a comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined by the organization's compensation philosophy and the experience of the selected candidate.

Search Process This search is being conducted by ND Leadership Partners, led by Managing Partner Chris Nguyen, as a retained executive search. Candidates will be evaluated through a structured process designed to assess executive leadership, strategic judgment, cultural competency, people leadership, relationship building, financial stewardship, governance partnership and the ability to lead through complexity and change.
Qualified candidates and referral sources are encouraged to engage with ND Leadership Partners. All expressions of interest will be managed with appropriate discretion and confidentiality throughout the search process.
Interested candidates are strongly encouraged to inquire promptly; applications received by Friday, September 11 will receive priority consideration and may be reviewed thereafter as the search continues. You can email Chris directly at Chris@nextdeavor.com.

Director of Operations

Georgia / Atlanta Cluster · DS Fitness

We’re growing fast, with nine gyms across two states already in the pipeline, and we’re hiring the operating leader who will make that build work. This is a builder’s seat, not a caretaker’s seat. You’ll take the operating system we run on our four Atlanta gyms, sharpen it into something we can trust and scale, and extend it as we integrate acquisitions and open new locations. This is your kind of role if you own a P&L by instinct, hold managers to a standard without being asked, and have run integrations or openings under a clock.

Reports to: 
Owner / Managing Member
Location: 
Metro Atlanta, in-field across all Georgia locations
Scope: 
5 Georgia gyms plus portfolio-wide financial ownership across all 9+ gyms in both states

ABOUT US

DS Fitness is a multi-unit Burn Boot Camp operator building toward and beyond a nine-gym portfolio across metro Atlanta and Upstate South Carolina. We run a disciplined operating model with a long-term institutional exit in view, and we care about financial rigor, accountability, and repeatable systems.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

·       The performance of the Atlanta cluster: five gyms, the GMs who run them, and the results they put up. You own how these gyms operate and grow.
·       Cluster NOI. It’s the number you’re accountable for, and you’ll have the authority to move it.
·       The financial backbone for all nine gyms: one set of numbers the whole group runs on, across both states.
WHAT YOU’LL DO

·       Run the gyms.
Spend real time in the locations, coach your GMs, set the standard, and hold it. Move each GM from “runs the gym” to “owns the P&L.”
·       Own the standard.
Set and hold the bar for member experience and facility standards across the cluster. Your GMs deliver it day to day. You make sure it stays consistent everywhere.
·       Own the number.
You’re accountable for cluster NOI. Drive membership, retention, conversion, and pricing across the gyms, and manage labor as a percentage of revenue.
·       Run a weekly cadence.
A standing operating rhythm and 1:1s on a scorecard, so every GM knows their numbers and you catch problems early.
·       Own the full SOP loop.
Spot the issue, build the fix, write the SOP, roll it out across the gyms, and hold each GM accountable for putting it in place within a set timeframe. Not just writing the playbook, but making sure the playbook actually gets run.
·       Use the data to stay ahead of problems.
Watch the numbers closely to catch issues as they start and correct them before they grow into real ones.
·       Find and stop the leaks.
The systemic ones that quietly cost real money: overstaffing, inefficient class schedules, missed transfers, sloppy promo execution.
·       Build the systems.
Own the SOP library, the reporting, and franchise and HQ compliance, so the cluster runs on numbers everyone trusts and nothing depends on someone remembering a rule. You own that financial backbone.
·       Open and integrate.
Lead the new locations openings and bring them and their teams up to standard. Each opening carries hard targets: presale goals hit by day 60, and at least 300 members within 90 days of grand opening.
·       Build the bench.
Own GM and staff hiring, onboarding, and retention.

WHAT YOU BRING

·       You’ve operated multiple locations and owned the results. You’ve carried a P&L, you read a number cold, and you notice when one looks wrong.
·       You lead people well. You hold managers to a standard and coach them to own their numbers without handholding.
·       You use data to catch problems early. You spot issues as they emerge and correct them before they become larger issues.
·       You’ve opened or integrated locations on a deadline, or you’re clearly ready to do so.
·       You’ve got the runway for this. Ideally seven or more years running multiple locations, and you’re ready to be in-market across metro Atlanta regularly, not running it from a desk.
·       You know membership or recurring-revenue businesses: churn, retention, conversion, and pricing.
No fitness background required. We welcome strong multi-unit operators from restaurant, retail, hospitality, boutique fitness, or any location-based service business. We’re hiring for the operating discipline.

WHAT WE’LL TEACH YOU

·       The Burn Boot Camp model, camp format, and programming.
·       Our tool stack (DOMO, POS and billing, franchise portal) and our specific SOPs.
·       The fitness product.
Not in this role: product standards, pricing strategy, capital, acquisitions, or vision.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

·       A trustworthy portfolio reporting layer and scorecard, built and live.
·       A GM accountability cadence that produces real P&L ownership across the cluster.
·       An acquisition integration executed to standard and the next new-location opening on track.

COMPENSATION

Target base of $120,000 to $140,000, plus a performance bonus of 20% to 30% of base tied to cluster NOI and the operating scorecard, with on-target earnings of roughly $150,000 to $175,000. Structure is weightable toward variable for the right operator.
